column1: # colloid.tsv — desktop icon name -> Colloid icon name
# The third column names artwork in the Colloid checkout (its own icon name,
# resolved through src/ + links/ by tools/vendor-colloid-icons.py).  A ``-``
# would mean "do not take this name from Colloid" and leaves it to the legacy
# Material/file-icon tables or the inherited theme -- there is no such row yet.
# This table is the whole system UI vocabulary of the theme: actions, status,
# devices, categories and the system applications.  Third-party applications
# are deliberately absent (they resolve to hicolor), and so are file types and
# --- actions: session / power, window and toolbar buttons ----------------------
# --- status: dialogs, NetworkManager, audio, panel indicators ------------------
# Cinnamon's notification applet loads these with icon_type=SYMBOLIC.
# Panel + tray names the applet asks for directly.
# --- devices: optical media, disks, printers, cameras, input -------------------
# --- categories: menu categories, preferences panels, legacy package_*/gnome-*/xfce_*/redhat_* names
# --- apps: system applications only (third-party apps fall through to hicolor) -
# Folders stay Material; the two trash names do not. Plank's Trash docklet and the
# Nemo/Cinnamon desktop trash ask for user-trash / user-trash-full, and a Material
# "folder-trash" reads as a folder in a 48 px dock slot. Colloid's can (and its
# full state) is the artwork those names actually mean.
